# Building Cross-Platform Tools

A key advantage of Rust is compile-once, run-anywhere ergonomics across Linux, macOS, and Windows. However, subtle operating system differences can easily break a CLI utility.

## Key Operating System Divergences

| Feature | Linux / Unix | macOS | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Path Separator** | `/` | `/` | `\` (or `/`) |
| **Line Ending** | `\n` (LF) | `\n` (LF) | `\r\n` (CRLF) |
| **Path Casing** | Case-sensitive | Case-preserving, insensitive | Case-insensitive |
| **File Permissions** | POSIX modes (`chmod`) | POSIX modes | Access Control Lists (ACLs) |
| **Pipes & Terminals** | POSIX TTY (`/dev/tty`) | POSIX TTY | Windows Console (`CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`) |

## Idiomatic Cross-Platform Patterns in Rust

### 1. Always Use `std::path::PathBuf` and Slices

Never concatenate file paths using string formatting like `format!("{}/{}", dir, file)`. Use `.join()`:

```rust
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

fn resolve_cache_file(base: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
    base.join("cache").join(name) // Evaluates to \ on Windows and / on Unix
}
```

### 2. Normalizing Line Endings

When parsing text data or comparing outputs, strip trailing carriage returns:

```rust
fn clean_line(raw: &str) -> &str {
    raw.strip_suffix("\r\n")
       .or_else(|| raw.strip_suffix('\n'))
       .unwrap_or(raw)
}
```

### 3. Conditional Compilation with `#[cfg(...)]`

When accessing OS-specific syscalls (e.g., Unix file permissions or Windows registry entries):

```rust
#[cfg(unix)]
fn set_executable_permission(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
    let mut perms = std::fs::metadata(path)?.permissions();
    perms.set_mode(0o755);
    std::fs::set_permissions(path, perms)
}

#[cfg(windows)]
fn set_executable_permission(_path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    // Windows file permissions rely on ACLs and executable extensions (.exe, .bat)
    Ok(())
}
```

## Cross-Compiling with `cross`

`cross` executes `cargo` commands inside curated Docker/Podman containers containing cross-toolchains:

```bash
# Build a fully static x86_64 Linux binary
cross build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --release

# Build for ARM64 Linux (Raspberry Pi / Graviton)
cross build --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl --release

# Build for Windows from Linux/macOS
cross build --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --release
```
